structural_memory.memory: Ordinary ship-shore connectivity has distinct owner/manager, vessel crew, shore IT/operations, terminal or antenna supplier, connectivity service provider or reseller, and port/shore-access roles. Equipment ownership, service entitlement, traffic policy and outage support can sit with different actors and should not be collapsed into one provider relationship.

Terminal or antenna readiness and communications-service readiness are separate lifecycle states. Hardware may be installed and powered while service is not activated or usable; conversely an active service contract does not prove that the onboard terminal path is operational.

Connectivity service itself has activation, suspension, renewal, entitlement and support states. A historical replay should distinguish contractual availability from observed session availability without retaining plan names, account details or provider-specific terms.

Coverage is time- and position-dependent availability rather than a timeless vessel attribute. Structural memory should preserve whether a path was expected, unavailable, intermittent or restored while exact footprints, beams, frequencies and coverage maps remain deferred to Evidence.

Nominal bandwidth or capacity and usable application throughput are different states. Shared-link contention, service policy, environmental path quality and competing operational or crew traffic can affect observed transfer performance without proving a fault in any application.

Latency, stability and continuity are distinct from simple connected/not-connected status. A link may remain technically available while becoming unsuitable for interactive remote support, large transfers or time-sensitive business processes.

Traffic purpose is a useful non-technical state boundary: safety/operational, business/administrative, maintenance/support and crew-welfare use can compete for constrained connectivity, but exact prioritization rules and configuration are not retained in blind Memory.

Redundancy should represent path independence and failover readiness rather than a count of radios or terminals. Multiple nominal paths may share equipment, power, shore infrastructure, service relationships or environmental exposure, so observed backup availability and tested switchover remain separate states.

Connectivity outage has a lifecycle: local observation, scope uncertainty, provider or shore acknowledgement, workaround or alternate-path use, restoration indication and vessel-side verification. Restoration announcements do not by themselves establish that all dependent transfers or applications recovered.

Port, coastal cellular or local wireless access can act as temporary supplemental connectivity with acquisition, authentication/authorization, handover and departure-loss states. This is structurally different from continuous ocean-going service and exact network details are deferred.

Data transfer has queue, partial-transfer, retry/resume, backlog and completion/acknowledgement states. A period of weak connectivity can create delayed shore visibility even after the underlying vessel observation or document existed, which matters for point-in-time known-time.

Remote maintenance/support, reporting, voyage/business workflows and digital recovery can depend on connectivity without connectivity being the root cause of the underlying equipment or software condition. Dependency failure and application/system failure should remain separately clocked.

Crew-welfare connectivity is operationally and economically distinct from distress/SAR communications and from business data use. Historical service availability or restrictions may affect welfare and retention experience, but this pass does not retain provider, price, usage-policy or vessel-specific claims.

P068 remote-vendor-connectivity state should separate authorization/session governance from the underlying communications path: approved remote support can still be impossible because connectivity is unavailable or too degraded, while an available link does not imply vendor access is authorized.

P062 distress/SAR communication readiness should not be used as evidence of ordinary broadband or business-connectivity readiness. Safety communications and general data services can have different equipment, service, coverage and operating assumptions.

P038 crew-welfare communication should distinguish service entitlement and traffic availability from the broader welfare outcome. A vessel can have connectivity capability while crew access is limited, degraded or unavailable for reasons not established in blind Memory.

P067 equipment lifecycle should treat communication terminals and antennas like other supported equipment while keeping service-contract, coverage and network-availability states outside the hardware condition record.
Remote-support dependency and alternate-path readiness partially overlap P068 defensive IT/OT recovery and vendor-support states.

Crew communications and safety-communications role separation overlaps prior welfare and distress/SAR passes; P069 adds the ordinary infrastructure/service layer rather than reclassifying those use cases.

reviewed_no_specific_memory: Exact frequencies, beams, satellite constellations, coverage maps, service plans, bandwidth commitments, latency figures and terminal configurations are intentionally not retained.
Named connectivity providers, resellers, antenna vendors, port Wi-Fi operators and vessel-by-vessel service histories require claim-scoped Evidence.
Exact outage incidents, restoration times, contractual SLA performance and current network availability require source-first Evidence and are not established here.
Private/regional provider lineages and historical non-English telecommunications terminology remain weak blind-recall areas and are deferred for later source archaeology.
negative_space: Exact radio/satellite/network engineering details, frequencies, credentials, configurations and coverage footprints.
Named service plans, pricing, quotas, SLA terms, providers, resellers and vessel installations.
Historical outage chronologies, provider-performance rankings and current connectivity posture.
Private/regional maritime telecom and managed-connectivity lineages plus non-English predecessor terminology.
epistemic_boundary: Memory-only connectivity lifecycle/orientation output. It is not navigation, communications, network, cyber, engineering or operational advice and does not establish any exact frequency, coverage, configuration, provider, service-plan, performance, outage, vessel-installation or current-readiness fact.
stop_reason: The ordinary ship-shore connectivity lifecycle is recalled at useful structural resolution and cleanly separated from distress/SAR, cyber access governance and crew-welfare outcomes. Further detail would become frequency-, coverage-map-, plan-, configuration-, provider-, vessel-, outage- or jurisdiction-specific and is deferred to claim-scoped Evidence.
